title: Dermatologists Say Sunscreen Is Necessary Year-Round. We Found the Best Ones to Buy—Starting at $10 - Women's Health
text: The 9 Best Sunscreens in 2026, According To Expert Testing About Women's Health Newsletter Subscribe My Bookmarks Women's Health+ Health Conditions Hub Shop Fitness Beauty Food Sports and Athletes Style Weight Loss Sex and Love Relationships Life Awards Follow Workout Routines Finder Health Other Editions Your Privacy Choices Privacy Notice Terms Of Use Skip to Content US US UK España Japan Newsletter Sign in Sign in Subscribe Search Sign in Sign in Subscribe US US UK España Japan Newsletter Sign in Sign in Subscribe Search Fitness Health Beauty Product Reviews Sports & Athletes Video Membership Perks About My Bookmarks Newsletter US Your Privacy Choices Privacy Notice Terms Of Use Fitness Health Beauty Product Reviews Sports & Athletes Video Membership Perks About More Beauty Skin The 9 Best Sunscreens of 2026, Tested by Dermatologists and Editors The 9 Best Sunscreens of 2026, Tested by Dermatologists and Editors Just in time for the last-minute holiday trips. By Nicole Saunders Updated: Nov 13, 2026 10:28 AM EST View Products Save Article Share Article JL Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us? I’ ve written extensively about sunscreen since 2019, most recently in our guide to SPF facts , spray sunscreen , and how one dermatologist uses it as a dry shampoo hack . But if you’re looking for a one-and-done power list of the best sunscreens of 2026, this is it. Best Sunscreens of 2026 Best Overall: Isdin Eryfotona Ageless SPF 50 ​ Best Budget: Neutrogena Beach Defense Sunscreen Stick SPF 50 ​ Best Mineral Sunscreen: EltaMD UV Daily Broad-Spectrum SPF 40 ​ Best for Exercise: La Roche-Posay Anthelios Melt-In Sunscreen Milk SPF 60 ​ Best Tinted Sunscreen: Tower 28 SunnyDays SPF 30 Tinted Sunscreen Foundation ​ So why am I low-key obsessed with wearing sunscreen? Allow dermatologist Gary Goldenberg, MD, to explain. “Daily sunscreen use is important for two main reasons: Skin cancer prevention and anti-aging,” he says. And the data backs him up. An Australian study tracked the skin of people who wore daily sunscreen regardless of weather and activities versus those who only wore SPF on sunny days or when they’re outdoors. The study evaluated their skin texture (microtopography) to evaluate aging and found that people who applied sunscreen daily aged significantly better than those who wore SPF occasionally. BRB, time to hit auto-subscribe on these Amazon sunscreens . And sunscreen’s benefits don’t stop there. Sun damage accumulates from daily activities like driving and sitting in front of a window, says dermatologist Hadley King, MD . That means even during the fall and winter, we should still double down on sunscreen. Here’s how to buy SPF like a dermatologist and beauty editor. Best Deal La Roche-Posay Anthelios Melt-In Sunscreen Milk SPF 60 $38 $28 NOW 25% OFF JUMP TO REVIEW Best Overall Isdin Eryfotona Ageless Tinted Mineral Sunscreen SPF 50 Best Overall Isdin Eryfotona Ageless Tinted Mineral Sunscreen SPF 50 $50 Amazon Also Consider $50 Dermstore Pros Unique DNA repair enzymes It helps with redness Lightweight formula absorbs quickly Water-resistant for active lifestyles Tinted and untinted options Cons Pricey, but there’s a smaller 1.7 fl. oz bottle to help ease the pain As a picky beauty editor, it really takes a lot for a product to truly impress me. Isdin Eryfotona Ageless Sunscreen has become a staple in my routine, and I will gladly continue repurchasing bottles to ensure my skin is protected for life. So what makes it stand out the most? The impressive ingredient list. Allow Dr. Goldenberg to explain. "Isdin's SPF contains ‘repairsomes,’ which help with reversing sun damage in skin cells," he says. That makes this a great pick for anyone with hyperpigmentation or sun spots, especially since the formula has a glowy, tinted finish. I had a light sunburn last summer, and my dermatologist suggested I use this SPF. After I slathered on moisturizer and layered on this liquid sunscreen during the day, I noticed my skin was less red after just two days. I was floored because I hadn’t used any new products other than the Isdin Eryfotona Ageless. A year later, and I can confirm it’s still well worth using. My skin never breaks out, the lightweight formula absorbs quickly, and it’s water-resistant for active lifestyles. It’s also available in tinted and untinted options. It absorbs in just a few minutes and mattifies my oily T-zone and leaves behind a soft, luminous finish. Not to mention, it doesn’t cause breakouts or irritate my skin when I’m dealing with seasonal changes and sensitivities. If I had to be nitpicky, then the only thing I dislike about Isdin is the price. However, there’s a smaller 1.7 fl. oz bottle to help ease the pain. I’ll continue to repurchase this sunscreen because it works fabulously with my oily, acne-prone skin. It’s also helpful for my 50-something mom’s mature skin. I also converted our visual editor, Jason Speakman, into a fan—he noticed a decrease in facial redness over six months of daily use. It's easy to apply or reapply, and it offers SPF 50 with water resistance, so people with active lifestyles really love it—just check the 10,208 perfect 5-star ratings on Amazon. Neutrogena is cheap, travel-friendly, glides on clear, and is effective. However, we found it was too greasy for oily skin. However, if you have normal or dry skin, or just want to glow, this is the face sunscreen for you. With festival season underway, your skin will definitely “shine bright like a diamond” with the help of this sunscreen. And honestly, at just under $10, it’s worth trying. Yes SPF Type Chemical SPF Level 50+ Active Ingredients Avobenzone (3%), homosalate (15%), octisalate (5%), and octocrylene (10%) Advertisement - Continue Reading Below Best Mineral Sunscreen EltaMD UV Daily Broad-Spectrum SPF 40 Best Mineral Sunscreen EltaMD UV Daily Broad-Spectrum SPF 40 $41 Amazon Also Consider $42 Walmart $30 Dermstore Pros Great for dry, sensitive skin types Loved by our editors and dermatologists Cons Will leave a white cast on darker skin tones Dr. Campbell is a fan of EltaMD's sunscreen, as are Lindsay Geller , Women's Health's lifestyle director, and Amanda Lucci, our special projects director. It contains hyaluronic acid, so Dr. Campbell often recommends it to patients with drier skin. EltaMD boasts a fragrance-free, paraben-free, and noncomedogenic formulation, making it ideal for sensitive and acne-prone skin. The lotion has a creamy, slightly whipped texture that requires a little extra effort to blend into the skin, but it’s worth it, says Geller. However, our editors with medium to dark skin tones say this leaves a white cast on their skin, but using the Tinted version can help. Features at a Glance Broad Spectrum? Yes SPF Type Mineral SPF Level 40 Active Ingredients Zinc oxide (9%) and octinoxate (7.5%) Best For Dry Skin La Roche-Posay Anthelios Melt-In Sunscreen Milk SPF 60 Best For Dry Skin La Roche-Posay Anthelios Melt-In Sunscreen Milk SPF 60 Now 25% Off $38 $28 Amazon Also Consider $19 Walmart $39 Ulta Beauty Pros Hydrates the skin Available at mass retailers Cons Can cause a whitecast if you apply too much La Roche-Posay is one of the most reliable skincare brands in the game. The line is a favorite of many dermatologists I consulted, and Dr. Ranella Hirsch, MD, highlights this particular sunscreen as her top pick. She highlights the creamy formulation, which hydrates her skin and leaves it feeling velvety soft. This is also Ritchey's new go-to. “As long as you don't smother yourself in it, I feel like it's pretty light for a sunscreen,” she says. “It's a little tacky after going on, but honestly, it was kind of nice—it definitely helped my makeup stick!” It also has a faint sunscreen smell, which she doesn't mind, since it reminds her that Anthelios Melt-In is working. She’s a self-described heavy sweater, and didn’t experience any streaking with this sunscreen. Just keep in mind that a little goes a long way—a lesson Ritchey learned the hard way. “The first time I put too much in my hand, I looked like Larry the Lifeguard from SpongeBob SquarePants. ” Dermatologists advise applying two finger-lengths of sunscreen—about a quarter-sized amount—to your face and neck. Features at a Glance SPF Level 60 SPF Type Chemical Active Ingredients Avobenzone (3%), homosalate (10%), octisalate (5%),  octocrylene (7%) Broad Spectrum? Yes Advertisement - Continue Reading Below Best Tinted Sunscreen Tower 28 SunnyDays SPF 30 Tinted Moisturizer Best Tinted Sunscreen Tower 28 SunnyDays SPF 30 Tinted Moisturizer $32 Amazon Also Consider $32 Sephora $32 Revolve Pros Best shade range Great for acne-prone skin Applies nicely with my fingers and brushes Cons Limited in very deep shades Tower 28 is one of the best sunscreens that I’ve ever used. It combines all of the benefits of a broad-spectrum mineral sunscreen with foundation-like coverage in 17 shades. It offers light-to-medium coverage that evens out my complexion without looking cakey or feeling goopy on my face. Problem spots like hyperpigmentation could use some extra love with concealer— Tower 28 makes a sweet one —but I don’t feel insecure if those spots show through with this sunscreen. It took me some trial and error to discover my exact shade, but I landed on the color 40 Silver Lake on my face and use 55 Temescal as a bronzer for a deep golden warmth. Application is also a breeze—it applies nicely with the warmth of my fingers, but I get the most coverage when using a densely packed brush like my BK Beauty 101 Foundation Brush . I just apply the SPF to my face, buff the fluffy bristles in small, circular motions across my face, and I experience zero streaks. Knowing that richer sunscreen shades can be a real let-down, I hit up digital designer Taryn Colbert to give this one a whirl. She uses the color 55 and puts its color payoff and longevity to the test. Tower 28 applies evenly to her bare skin and feels like nothing is on her face. Since she doesn’t have any texture or acne issues, she didn’t notice any splotches or separation with extra oil. I also have oily skin and noticed some pore emphasis on my cheeks after a few hours of wear, but honestly, touching up with oil-blotting sheets and a thin, fresh layer of SPF helps. While Colbert and I agree with Tower 28’s sentiment that the colors are flexible, it would still be nice to have a wider range of undertones in the tan and deep shades. Still, it’s the SPF that replaces my foundation each summer and one I recommend to anyone who doesn’t want to compromise on sun protection or cosmetic coverage. Features at a Glance Broad-spectrum? Yes SPF Type Mineral SPF Level 30 Key Ingredients Zinc oxide (12.6%) Best For Easy Reapplication Brush On Block SPF 50 Mineral Powder Sunscreen Best For Easy Reapplication Brush On Block SPF 50 Mineral Powder Sunscreen $46 Amazon Credit: Justin Steele Pros Easy to reapply over makeup Dermatologist-approved dry shampoo hack Portable design Refillable Cons Only available in 2 shades Powder sunscreen is the most underrated formulation—and Brush on Block is my favorite. It comes in a tube that features soft bristles that I dust over my face like a setting powder. It’s mess-free, making it ideal for touch-ups on the go. The broad-spectrum sunscreen is also water-resistant, so I can dust it on while poolside without worry. But above all, it earned major snaps from Dr. King, who uses it on her face and scalp as a dry shampoo hack. Beyond perking up your hair by absorbing oil, it can add volume and texture by coating your strands with fine powders, making your hair appear fuller without sticky residue, says Dr. Goldenberg. So how should you apply it? Dr. King likes to gently rub or massage the powder into the scalp with her fingertips so that it’s not visible, she says. The only downside? There is only one shade available: Translucent. It hasn’t left my caramel complexion looking ghostly. However, the brand makes other tinted powder sunscreens. I’d appreciate it if this SPF 50 became available in richer shades to accommodate more melanin-rich complexions and anyone with dark hair like mine. Ultraviolet radiation from the sun falls into two categories: ultraviolet A (UVA) and ultraviolet B (UVB). UVA rays cause signs of aging, such as hyperpigmentation, lines, and wrinkles. Meanwhile, UVB rays can cause more serious damage, including sunburn and skin cancer. Your safest bet is to only use broad-spectrum sunscreens to help protect against UVA and UVB rays. Mineral vs. Chemical Sunscreen: Which Is Better? Next, choose either a mineral or a chemical sunscreen. Here’s more insight to help you determine between the two formulations. Is mineral sunscreen actually better? Active ingredients are zinc oxide and titanium dioxide. Tinted mineral sunscreens contain iron oxides, which can help reduce hyperpigmentation. How do mineral sunscreens work? They create a physical barrier that reflects and scatters UV rays away from the skin’s surface, says dermatologist Divya Shokeen, MD . Pros: Mineral sunscreens offer instant broad-spectrum protection, says dermatologist Caren Campbell, MD . They are also safer for sensitive and acne-prone skin. Another bonus of using a physical sunscreen is that its ingredients are safer to use during pregnancy . Cons: Mineral sunscreens are more likely to leave behind a cast on melanin-rich complexions. What is a chemical-based sunscreen? Active ingredients are avobenzone, homosalate, octisalate, and octocrylene. How do they work? "Chemical filters absorb the sun's rays, deflecting their damage by turning them into heat," says Dr. Shokeen. Pros: They are acne-safe and tend to be easier to rub in and for the skin to absorb, says dermatologist Sheila Farhang, MD . They’re also less likely to leave behind an ashy finish on Brown and Black skin. Cons: They can irritate sensitive skin and require a 15-to-20-minute waiting period before being effective against sun exposure. TL;DR They both have benefits and limitations, but ultimately, the best one is the sunscreen you’ll actually use and reapply. As for me? Well, I like both types. However, I typically use mineral sunscreen on my face, so I can head outside immediately after work instead of lingering for the approximately 15-minute waiting period associated with chemical sunscreens. What are the best ingredients found in a good sunscreen? Broad-spectrum coverage, sunscreen type, and SPF coverage are the big three considerations. But another factor worth emphasizing is other non-active skincare ingredients that will help bolster your complexion. Dermatologist Elyse Love, MD, is a big fan of niacinamide to calm the skin and improve its tone and texture. Also, look for ingredients that support your skin type and goals. For example, if you want to brighten your complexion, you'll look for a sunscreen with vitamin C . If you have dry skin, seek out hydrating ingredients like hyaluronic acid .
